author: Claude
headline: US futures bounce 2% after last week's rout as a shortened Thanksgiving week begins
summary: After an 8.6% fall in the S&P 500 last week, markets are steadier this morning. S&P 500 futures are up about 2%, the FTSE 100 is up 0.4% and Germany's DAX 0.5%, and the VIX fear gauge has eased 13% to 31.2. Traders have also dropped bets on a big half-point Fed rate rise in December after the sell-off. One good morning doesn't end a correction, though: the S&P 500 is still 6% below its 200-day average, so the picks stay defensive. US markets are shut on Thursday for Thanksgiving, so trading may be thin this week.
points: The picks are unchanged from Friday: Visa, Coca-Cola, Tesco, Johnson & Johnson and the US healthcare fund (XLV). Altria, AbbVie and Gilead are still rated 'good buy'.
London's biggest fallers from Friday are leading the bounce: Rolls-Royce is up 1.7%, HSBC 1.5%, Glencore 1.5% and Anglo American 1.4%. Vodafone is down 2.5%.
Gold is up 2.7% to about $3,610 after last week's slide. Oil is down 1.4% to $82.80, even after Yemen's Houthis claimed attacks on a Saudi oil refinery.
Tech is still the weakest sector, and new US probes into the Nvidia chip-smuggling case keep chip stocks under a cloud.
Bitcoin is up 0.5% at about $61,500, but every major cryptocurrency is still in a downtrend.
